summary:
Batch 3 (software only). Four files, no research runner and no fpga/RTL touched.

1) scripts/platform.py - added exactly one run() statement to bench() (lines 167-168 are the existing platform_timeout.c compile; the new 2-line statement mirrors it and compiles bench/platform_sd_update.c -> out/bench/platform-sd-update with the same -O2 -static -Wall -Wextra flags and no -I uapi header path). No other hunk.

2) scripts/build_update_software.py (new) - imports platform.py via importlib (module name cpn_platform), sets platform.ENV['LOCALVERSION']='-cpn2-net1', and drives the real build with platform.kernel(12) then platform.firmware(12). Before building: ensure_previous() snapshots the cpn1 run products (out/linux/.../Image, out/linux/platform.dtb, out/rootfs.cpio, out/opensbi/.../fw_payload.bin) and the cpn1 state (out/paper-route-review-20261004/software-build-state.json) into out/software-update-20261004/previous, but only when previous/ does not yet exist; a previous-manifest.json records source paths, sizes and sha256 and flags any missing source. capture_inputs() records sha256+size for the declared input groups (config, dts, driver, firmware, rootscripts, tool) using an explicit/glob path table; it never reads local.json or any other secret (state carries secrets_excluded=true). After the build it enforces the three failure conditions: fw_payload.bin > 33554432 bytes -> fail; a critical config not 'y' (CONFIG_RISCV, CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD) or an empty CONFIG_INITRAMFS_SOURCE -> fail; a missing/empty delivery tool (out/bench/platform-sd-update) -> fail. On success it copies Image, platform.dtb, rootfs.cpio, fw_payload.bin and the platform-sd-update tool run package into the independent out/software-update-20261004/delivery with a per-artifact sha256 manifest. It never runs check() or fpga(); state records source_mode='authorized_working_tree', check_bypassed='authorized_software_working_tree', fpga='not_run'. The state file out/software-update-20261004/software-update-state.json is written atomically and goes running -> complete/failed; on any exception it records the original exit (subprocess returncode when present) and re-raises the original exception unchanged, and finished_at is always written in a finally block. The module prints nothing and never redirects stdout/stderr (only platform.run's own '+ cmd' lines reach the caller's stream).

3) scripts/mac_update_reboot.py (new) - external reboot path. Default is dry-run: no serial, no process, no filesystem writes, and pyserial is not imported (import serial lives only inside default_serial_factory). --run requires an explicit local non-empty --bit, --port, --expected-kernel and a fresh --out with no defaults, so there is no port scan and no BIT auto-selection; a bad bit/args or an existing --out raises SystemExit before anything is created. A single Console owns the serial link for the whole run (one open, one close). It sends 'sync; echo <IDMA-REBOOT-...>' and waits for a line whose stripped content is exactly the token, so the terminal echo of the command line can never be accepted as confirmation. A short drain clears leftover output, then it runs openFPGALoader with a fixed argv ['openFPGALoader','-b','genesys2','--freq','1000000',<BIT>] - no flash write and no SD access. It then reads the boot UART until a login prompt or shell prompt (handling login/password prompts), captures uname -r and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id via unique start/end marker lines, and only declares success when uname -r verbatim equals --expected-kernel AND boot_id is non-empty; a bare boot-log marker is never used as evidence. uart.log keeps every UART byte plus outbound lines, fpga-load.stdout/stderr keep the loader output, and result.json (schema mac-update-reboot-v1) is written in a finally block for both complete and failed runs; any error stops the run with no retry and no resume.

4) tests/test_mac_update_reboot.py (new) - 9 unittest cases that mock the entire serial link, process runner, clock and sleeper through main() keyword injection (no real serial/JTAG/subprocess). Coverage: dry-run makes no external writes and opens no port; missing port/bit/kernel/out and an existing out are refused; the command echo alone is not accepted as the sync token; an openFPGALoader failure stops on the first attempt and records returncode 1; a boot/prompt timeout stops; a uname mismatch fails; an empty boot_id fails; and success requires both the exact kernel and a non-empty boot_id with the fixed loader argv.

Assumptions to verify (flagged, not silently resolved):
- bench/platform_sd_update.c is provided by the parallel worker and needs no -I uapi include (mirrors platform_timeout.c); if it includes linux/idma.h the bench() line must gain '-I', uapi.
- INPUT_PATTERNS['firmware'] uses globs (opensbi/platform/fpga/ariane/platform.c, opensbi/lib/utils/reset/*.c) because the exact fdt_reset_init() file was not supplied; wrong paths only show as an empty group plus a note in the state, they do not fail the build. The driver group also globs linux/drivers/net/ethernet/lowrisc/** for the parallel lowrisc_ethernet driver.
- REQUIRED_CONFIG_Y is (CONFIG_RISCV, CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD); add the driver-specific config name once Codex confirms it.
- openFPGALoader argv uses '--freq 1000000' as two tokens (task text was '--freq1000000'); confirm against the installed openFPGALoader --help.
- previous/ sources come from the current out/ artifacts plus out/paper-route-review-20261004/software-build-state.json; a missing source is recorded, not fatal, so a path drift will not abort the snapshot.

No tests were executed in this session; the checks below are for Codex to run and to confirm.
